title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
excerpt: AI wearables, such as smart glasses, extend the context available to agents beyond digital environments to users' physical surroundings. With these devices, computer tasks can originate from users' ongoing activities rather than solely from explicit instructions. Through first-person observations, agents can identify objects and activities relevant to user requests and ground digital tasks in the surrounding context. We call this interaction paradigm Ego Use. However, first-person observations are limited by the wearer's viewpoint and may provide incomplete or ambiguous evidence of ongoing activities. As new observations arrive, agents may need to revise their understanding of the physical…

ai.summary: EgoUseBench is a benchmark that evaluates computer‑use agents that operate from first‑person wearable observations, testing how they handle tasks grounded in a user's physical context.
ai.why: It provides a standard for measuring and improving agents that integrate AR/VR wearables with digital workflows.

title: AIRIS: Benchmarking Social Embodied Intelligence in Egocentric Streaming Videos
excerpt: Embodied agents operating around people must not only recognize social cues, but also decide when the available evidence is sufficient, whether to intervene, and how to respond without violating social norms. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate these abilities in isolation or with access to completed videos, obscuring where an online social decision fails. We introduce AIRIS, a causal streaming benchmark that formulates social embodied intelligence as a time-anchored chain of Attention, Intention, Reaction, and Interaction (A-I-R-I). AIRIS contains 8,000 expert-curated questions grounded in 357 egocentric clips across 11 context categories and 36 capability dimensions. At each query…

ai.summary: AIRIS is a causal streaming benchmark that evaluates social embodied intelligence by requiring agents to make time‑anchored decisions in egocentric videos, testing attention, intent, and response under social norms.
ai.why: Provides a realistic testbed for developers building socially aware embodied agents.

title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
excerpt: Establishing effective scaling laws for medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains a persistent and fundamental challenge. Our systematic evaluation shows that existing medical MLLMs tend to underperform frontier general-purpose MLLMs across a range of medical tasks, while scaling model size primarily improves text capabilities rather than multimodal perception, and enabling reasoning modes fails to close this visual gap. To investigate how medical multimodal intelligence scales in practice, we introduce Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model with 3B activated parameters, built by combining stage-specific curation over 322.7 million candidate records with a…

ai.summary: Sage‑Med presents scaling experiments on medical multimodal large language models, finding that larger model sizes improve text tasks but do not close the visual perception gap compared to frontier general‑purpose LLMs.
ai.why: The results guide developers on where scaling effort yields returns and where architectural changes are needed for medical vision tasks.

title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
excerpt: Learning for dexterous manipulation is limited by the scarcity of high-quality demonstrations: retargeting from human video is imprecise, teleoperation gives no force feedback to the operator, and exoskeleton-based collection is hard to scale up. We present PyRUA-Dex, a framework that enables coding agents to develop dexterous manipulation through programmatic policy, without the need of demonstrations. The programmatic policy is developed in two stages: during exploration, multiple agents explore in parallel for task skills and ways to compose them, and a distilling agent condenses the successful attempts into a task library and one program. During refinement, this program is improved…

ai.summary: PyRUA‑Dex introduces a framework where coding agents learn programmatic policies for dexterous bimanual manipulation without human demonstrations, using exploration and refinement stages.
ai.why: Enables developers to create high‑precision robotic control software via code generation rather than costly data collection.

title: High-Fidelity Image Matting with Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
excerpt: Diffusion models have shown strong potential for image matting by transferring generative priors learned from large-scale pretraining. However, existing approaches largely rely on latent diffusion models, whose compressed representations and VAE-based reconstruction introduce a mismatch with the high-frequency precision required for matting. We present PixelMatte, a framework that adapts pretrained pixel-space diffusion transformers for high-fidelity image matting. We show that strong image-conditioned matting capabilities can be acquired even from a pure text-to-image model without paired image-to-image pretraining. Our approach reuses the backbone's native patch embedding to jointly…

ai.summary: PixelMatte is a new framework that adapts pretrained pixel‑space diffusion transformers for high‑fidelity image matting, avoiding the low‑frequency limitations of latent diffusion models.
ai.why: The method can be used to build more accurate matting tools in graphics and vision pipelines.

title: Entangle: Scaling Human-Video In-Context World-Action Models across Unseen Tasks and Contexts
excerpt: In-context learning (ICL) enables foundation models to perform unseen tasks from context without parameter updates. In robotic manipulation, a human video provides the context that specifies how a task should be performed. However, scaling human-video ICL on world-action models (WAMs) faces two challenges: task-level human-robot pairs are not temporally aligned with robot actions, and standard action losses allow policies to rely on initial-scene or task-identity shortcuts rather than tracking the context. We present Entangle, an in-context world-action model that maps a single human video and current robot observations to future visual states and executable actions. To scale temporally…

ai.summary: The paper introduces Entangle, a world-action model that uses in‑context learning from human videos to perform robotic manipulation tasks without fine‑tuning, addressing misalignment between human‑robot video pairs and shortcut learning in action losses.
ai.why: It shows how to leverage unaligned human video data for more generalizable robot policies, which developers can adapt for flexible robot control pipelines.

title: Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation
excerpt: Real-time autoregressive video generators stream minutes of video and accept new prompts on the fly, but struggle to keep people, objects, and places consistent over a long interactive story. Agent systems provide such memory for offline multi-shot generation, yet they read the whole script in advance, plan each shot before generating it, and regenerate failed shots, which a live stream does not allow. We present Agentic LongLive, an asynchronous agentic memory for long video generation. A memory agent on separate GPUs reads only the prompts revealed so far, never the generated video, and keeps a text state and evolving images for every person, object, and scene. From this entity memory it…

ai.summary: Agentic LongLive introduces an asynchronous agentic memory system that lets real-time autoregressive video generators maintain consistent people, objects, and places over long interactive stories without pre‑reading the entire script.
ai.why: It enables developers building live video generation tools to keep narrative coherence across extended streams.

title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
excerpt: Looped Transformers boost expressivity by reusing shared layers across loops, yet at the cost of efficiency. Pushing their expressivity-efficiency frontier requires rethinking the core mechanism connecting adjacent loops: What should be passed as a Transformer loops? We introduce Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), whose Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) uses keys and values (KV) as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops. Under loop residual, MoLT-R retains the residual stream and reads local KV across loops for expressivity. Under loop KV, MoLT-KV instead restarts from embeddings and reads current-loop local KV with preceding-loop memory KV at earlier positions for efficiency…

ai.summary: The Mixture‑of‑Loops Transformer (MoLT) introduces Mixture‑of‑Loops Attention, using keys and values as reusable memory across transformer loops to improve expressivity without sacrificing efficiency.
ai.why: Developers can adopt MoLT to build deeper or loop‑based models that retain performance while reducing compute overhead.

title: Playfulness as Feedback for Agentic Game Development
excerpt: Coding agents can generate runnable games from natural-language descriptions. However, a runnable game does not guarantee an excellent gameplay experience for players. In our view, a playful game should provide 1) reliable core functionality, 2) appealing visual design and assets, and 3) rich gameplay that supports exploration and progression. How agents can improve these aspects of playfulness remains underexplored. In our work, we propose Play2Evolve, a recursive game development framework with three stages: Initialization, Refinement, and Evolution. Using playfulness as feedback, agents playtest the game and diagnose issues in its functionality, visual presentation, and gameplay. Their…

ai.summary: Play2Evolve is a recursive framework where a coding agent iteratively refines a game’s core functionality, visual assets, and gameplay depth, using playfulness as feedback to improve generated games.
ai.why: Offers a concrete pipeline for developers to automate game creation and iterative quality improvement.

title: DyLoMo-DiT: Dynamic Looped Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Transformers
excerpt: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) scale model capacity by increasing both parameter count and computation. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants expand parameter capacity while keeping per-token computation roughly fixed, but still require substantial parameter storage. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Looped MoE DiT (DyLoMo-DiT), which reuses parameters rather than adding them: a weight-shared loop repeatedly applies the middle layers, while sparse experts allocate parameter capacity across tokens. This design deepens the network without adding parameters, freeing the parameter budget for other uses, such as more experts or more distinct layers. It also allocates compute dynamically, varying the…

ai.summary: DyLoMo-DiT proposes a Dynamic Looped Mixture‑of‑Experts diffusion transformer that reuses middle‑layer weights in a weight‑shared loop and adds sparse experts, increasing parameter capacity while keeping per‑token compute stable.
ai.why: Developers can train larger diffusion models with lower memory overhead, enabling more powerful generative applications.

title: Target-Part Preference Optimization for Part-Aware 3D Generation
excerpt: Part-aware 3D generation requires not only globally plausible objects but also complete, well-separated semantic parts, yet high-quality part decompositions remain too scarce to support large-scale supervised fine-tuning. We study whether preference fine-tuning based on Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) can adapt a pretrained part-aware generator from limited part-annotated data without architectural changes. We rank candidates generated with different random seeds against ground-truth (GT) geometric metrics, and select the (object, target-part) examples with the largest across-seed quality gap. Each selected example stores a seed pair whose two flow trajectories share one clean GT…

ai.summary: The paper proposes using Direct Preference Optimization to fine‑tune a pretrained part‑aware 3D generator on limited part‑annotated data, improving semantic part separation without changing the model architecture.
ai.why: Developers can improve 3D generation quality for applications like CAD or gaming using small labeled datasets.

title: DocSEAM: Bidirectional Cross-Page Encoding for Multi-Page Document Understanding
excerpt: Multi-page document vision-language models encode each page independently, creating a feature-level discontinuity at page boundaries: visual tokens are formed without access to content on adjacent pages, and the language model must reason over these page representations formed in isolation. We introduce DocSEAM (Document Selective Enrichment via Anchored Masking), a lightweight module inserted between a pretrained vision encoder and the language model that injects the inductive bias of local cross-page context into visual representations. For each page, DocSEAM forms a local triplet with its two neighbors, applies center-anchored masked self-attention with directional salience gates to fuse…

ai.summary: DocSEAM is a lightweight module inserted between a pretrained vision encoder and language model that injects cross‑page visual context via anchored masking, improving multi‑page document understanding.
ai.why: It enables developers to build better V‑L systems for PDFs and scanned books without retraining large models.

title: VibeVideoAgent: Closing the Perceptual Loop for Code-Driven Video Generation
excerpt: Code-driven video generation asks a coding agent to write and run rendering programs. This gives exact control over typography, data visualizations, synchronized audio, and multi-shot scenes, and it leaves an editable project behind. A program that exits cleanly can still render overlapping labels, a camera aimed away from its subject, broken object interactions, or narration that drifts out of sync, and none of these raise a runtime error. Feeding rendered frames and audio back into the coding session bloats its long-horizon context, while critiquing only the finished full-resolution render turns early design mistakes into costly rewrites. We introduce VibeVideoAgent, a training-free…

ai.summary: VibeVideoAgent proposes a coding‑agent loop that generates video by writing rendering code, runs it, and feeds the resulting frames and audio back into the agent for iterative improvement.
ai.why: It offers a concrete framework for developers to build controllable, editable video generation pipelines driven by code rather than black‑box diffusion models.

title: Let Vision-Language Models Generate Images through Their Representations
excerpt: Recent unified multimodal models aim to combine visual understanding and generation within a single model, yet effectively integrating the two capabilities remains challenging. Leveraging pretrained vision-language models offers a way to build on already learned multimodal knowledge, but making this knowledge effectively accessible to visual generation remains nontrivial. We find that a central challenge lies in the heterogeneous visual representations used for understanding and generation. To address this challenge, we introduce Integral, which converts a pretrained vision-language model into a unified multimodal model by constructing a shared visual representation space across the two…

ai.summary: The authors propose a method for vision‑language models to generate images by reusing their internal multimodal representations, bridging the gap between understanding and synthesis in unified models.
ai.why: Enabling image generation from existing VL models could simplify building multimodal applications without training separate generators.

title: FoundSurface: Feedforward Ray-Based 3D Scene Surface Reconstruction from Unposed Images
excerpt: Accurate 3D surface reconstruction from unposed images remains a fundamental challenge in computer vision. Recent feed-forward pointmap methods eliminate the need for camera poses but inherently produce discrete, sparse representations. In this paper, we present a generalizable pipeline that directly recovers continuous, high-fidelity 3D surfaces from unposed images by seamlessly integrating pointmap- and ray-based representations. Our approach first extracts explicit geometric priors using a pre-trained pointmap model. A query-view-centric selection module then identifies geometrically relevant reference views via a robust surfel voting mechanism. Next, a cross-attention regressor bridges…

ai.summary: FoundSurface presents a feed‑forward pipeline that combines point‑map and ray‑based representations to reconstruct continuous, high‑fidelity 3D surfaces directly from unposed images.
ai.why: Enables developers to obtain accurate 3D models without needing camera pose estimation, simplifying 3D reconstruction pipelines.

title: Real2SimLab: A Unified Platform for Real-to-Simulation Transfer
excerpt: Real-to-simulation transfer, which builds simulations from real-world observations, has long been studied in research and industry. Recently, coding agents have become capable of generating simulation programs from video recordings, and several benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate them. However, each individual benchmark defines its own inputs, deliverables, and scoring pipeline. This leads to N times M integrations when evaluating N methods on M benchmarks. To this end, we present Real2SimLab, a unified platform for real-to-simulation transfer. It evaluates a method by running its written program and scoring the output simulation with the original scorer of each benchmark. Moreover…

ai.summary: The authors introduce Real2SimLab, a unified platform that standardizes inputs, outputs, and evaluation pipelines for real-to-simulation transfer benchmarks, eliminating the need for separate integrations across methods and benchmarks.

title: Improving and Expanding Video Editing Capabilities Without Videos
excerpt: Image editing models can follow a wide range of instructions, but video editing models still lag behind, limited in part by the difficulty of collecting paired source and edited videos. We introduce Image-to-Video Transfer (I2VT), which improves pretrained video editors and expands them to new editing tasks using an image editor. It enables efficient post-training with no architectural changes and no new videos, using only individual images. Our key idea is to let the video editor role-play as an image editor: it edits an image as a one-frame video, with the image editor guiding the…

ai.summary: The paper introduces Image-to-Video Transfer (I2VT), a method that upgrades pretrained video editors with capabilities from image editors without needing new paired video data, using post‑training only and no architectural changes.

title: HOG-WAM: Improving Visual Robustness through Future Gradient Prediction
excerpt: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet visual corruption can disrupt the resulting policies. We introduce HOG-WAM, which adds future Histograms of Oriented Gradients (HOG) as structural supervision derived directly from demonstration images. An auxiliary HOG diffusion transformer (DiT) module reads RGB features through asymmetric attention, allowing its objective to shape the visual representation used for control. The module is used only during training and removed at inference, preserving FastWAM's RGB-to-action architecture.
